Luke 13:19 uses it in the mustard seed parable, where a man plants a seed in 'his garden.' The word carries rich symbolic resonance in Greek and Jewish tradition—from the gardens of Adonis to the Garden of Eden—making its New Testament appearances at arrest and resurrection quietly profound. All major translations agree: Spanish 'huerto,' French 'jardin,' German 'Garten.'"
